messages:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to finalize the deprecation window for /v1 endpoints and decide where the compatibility shim lives. Two main options: gateway-level shim (in our API gateway) or an opt-in client-side proxy that customers can run. Pros/cons below, looking for engineering + product tradeoffs.

Mira: Gateway shim = easiest for customers (zero change) but risk: adds per-request latency + hard to reason about edge cases when models diverge. Also complicates routing rules. :thinking_face:

Jon: If we do gateway shim, can we make it configurable per-tenant? Some enterprise customers will insist on explicit opt-in. Can we use header toggles like `x-rw-compat: v1`?

Sam: Yeah we were thinking per-tenant flag and also a runtime toggle. Header idea makes sense for gradual rollout. Example transform prototype:
```
# pseudo-transform in gateway (lua-like)
if req.headers["x-rw-client-v"] == "1" then
  req.path = req.path:gsub("/v1/", "/v2/")
  -- translate legacy auth header
  req.headers["authorization"] = transform_legacy(req.headers["x-legacy-auth"])
end
```

Eva: The tricky piece is semantics: v1 allowed implicit truncation of function args and v2 enforces strict schema. Shim must be able to detect and rewrite payloads or fallback to v1 model runtime. That gets hairy fast.

Jon: Could we instead deploy a thin compatibility runtime behind v2 routes that accepts v1 shape and proxies to a v1-compatible handler? Keeps gateway simple and pushes complexity to servicer.

Mira: That's basically a per-model compatibility adapter. I like it because the runtime can use existing model adapters and tests. Downsides: more components to operate and we need capacity for both v1 and v2 semantics during migration.

Sam: Operation cost is real. Product asked for a 6-month deprecation window. We should instrument usage by `x-rw-client-v` header to see % of traffic still on v1. If usage drops below 0.5% for 30d, we auto-cut. Add a rate-limited fallback to avoid sudden failures.

Eva: For testing, we should have an eval suite that runs v1 prompts against v2 model+shim and compares outputs. If quality regression > threshold, block auto-switch. This avoids silent regressions.

deploy-bot: canary/shim-v1-router deployed to canary cluster (svc/shim-compat-canary) — 8 instances. Logs forwarded to /infra/shim-canary.

Jon: Operational checklist suggestion: 
- metrics: header count, transformed payloads, latency p50/p95 delta, error rate
- rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global
- kill-switch: tenant-level and global flags
- tests: unit + synthetic eval harness

Mira: One more policy decision: do we accept security-sensitive translations in-shim (e.g., rewriting auth headers)? If not, we force customers to migrate auth headers before cutover. Security team input required.

Sam: Agreed — @Eva can you sync with security? Also product to confirm 6-month window. Ops: add logging for any shim rewrite (redact tokens) so we can audit.

Eva: I'll take security POV. Short term recommend: no auth transforms in gateway. Use adapter runtime for anything that touches credentials.

Sam: Action items:
- Eva: security call + final guidance by EOD Tue
- Jon: prototype adapter service resource estimate and cost delta by Fri
- Mira: spec for metrics & rollout automation (feature flag gates) by next Wed
- Infra: ensure canary logging retention is 30d for this experiment

Mira: Also propose we add a deprecation notice header in responses for any v1 traffic: `Warning: Redwood v1 deprecating in 180 days; see https://redwood.ai/migrate` :warning:

Sam: Solid. Will summarize and send to product + PMs. Thanks all. :rocket:
